label: trial after an a1 rare-unrewarded outcome (evidence S1 is good): D1, and D2 on reaching S1 via a1
explanation: Reset-gate unit 15 is never active at GO, never active with reward input 1, and never active when a2 was chosen (in_action 2 or state S2 at D2: zero activations). It fires on the trial right after the agent chose a1, took the rare transition to S2 and was not rewarded. Under model-based reasoning that outcome means S1 is good, so the agent should stay on a1. The unit fires at that trial D1 (unrewarded input shown); this is the strongest activation, holding 82% of the top-quartile mass. It also fires at D2 if the agent repeats a1 and reaches S1 (precision 0.91 for that clause alone). The predicate uses only observed variables. Dev: P 0.79, R 0.64, F1 0.70, mass recall 0.75. Most of the misses are weak D2 activations on a1->S1 common steps in other contexts, especially after unrewarded trials. Some misses sit at window-start D1/D2 steps where the previous trial is outside the window. A broader predicate, (D2 & a1 & S1) | (D1 & prev a1 rare unrewarded), reaches 93% recall but its precision is only 0.34. So the weak firing spreads over a1->S1 D2 steps generally, while the strong firing is specific to the rare-unrewarded-a1 history. Lone D1 r0 after a common a1->S1 unrewarded trial fires weakly at most.
